tests.name: test_against_counting
tests.description: On 300 random sorted lists of up to 10 whole numbers from 1 to 6, with many repeats, it agrees with counting the items one by one, for ends below, inside and above the list, low above high among them.

tests.name: test_edges
tests.description: An empty list, a range around every item, a low equal to the high, and a low above the high.

tests.name: test_looks
tests.description: On a sorted list of a million even numbers it gives the right counts, looking at no more than 42 different items each time.
tests.message: For the million even numbers from 0 to 1,999,998, count_between(xs, 1000, 3000) gives 1,000, not 1,001.

tests.name: test_starts_empty
tests.description: A new HashSet has a list of 8 empty buckets, and len 0.

tests.name: test_example
tests.description: After adding 3, 11, 19, 27 and 13, bucket 3 holds [3, 11, 19, 27] and bucket 5 holds [13]; 19 is in the set, 35 is not, and len gives 5.

tests.name: test_like_a_set
tests.description: Adding 60 random whole numbers from 0 to 40, many of them more than once, gives the same answers to in and len as Python's own set.

tests.name: test_strings
tests.description: Strings are keys too: each word added is found once, and other words are not found.

tests.name: test_doubles
tests.description: The buckets double when a new key would make the keys outnumber them: 8 buckets for up to 8 keys, 16 for 9 to 16, 32 for 17 to 32 and 64 for 33 to 40, and adding a key again changes nothing.
tests.message: With 9 keys the set has 8 buckets, not 16. Double the buckets only when a new key, not one already there, would make the keys outnumber them.

tests.name: test_moved
tests.description: After 43 different keys the buckets have doubled to 64, and every key is in bucket hash(key) % 64, once only, and the buckets are all different lists.
tests.message: After adding 43 different keys the set has 8 buckets, not 64, so this check cannot see whether keys move when the buckets double. Double the buckets when a new key would make the keys outnumber them.

tests.name: test_one_bucket
tests.description: A lookup compares the key only with the keys in its own bucket: looking up a key that was never added, among 40 keys, compares it with no more keys than that bucket holds.

tests.name: test_configs
tests.description: Keys of a class whose __hash__ agrees with its __eq__ work: two equal configs count once.

tests.name: test_find_runs
tests.description: find_runs([3, 5, 2, 2, 7, 1]) gives [[3, 5], [2, 2, 7], [1]], and it handles an empty list, one item, a list that only falls, and equal items, which stay in one run.

tests.name: test_small
tests.description: run_sort gives [] for an empty list, and [7] for a list holding the one item 7.

tests.name: test_in_order
tests.description: A list of 1,000 items already in order is one run, so run_sort gives it back in order after 999 comparisons.

tests.name: test_sorts
tests.description: On 300 random lists of 0 to 12 losses, each a whole number from 1 to 4 so that many are equal, run_sort gives the losses in order, each item once, and equal losses in the order they came.

tests.name: test_pairs
tests.description: On 512 shuffled losses it makes at most 5,120 comparisons: merging the runs in pairs, round after round, keeps the work close to merge sort's.

tests.name: test_new_list
tests.description: run_sort gives a new list, and leaves the list it was given as it was, even when that list is already in order.

tests.name: test_own_work
tests.description: run_sort does the sorting itself: neither it nor any function it calls uses Python's sorted or a list's sort.

tests.name: test_example
tests.description: bisect_left([10, 20, 30], 25) is 2, the slot where 25 would go.
tests.message: Stopped on line 5, in bisect_left: The code ran for too long and was stopped. Is there a loop that never ends, or code that runs a very large number of times?

tests.name: test_against_bisect
tests.description: On 300 random sorted lists of up to 10 whole numbers from 1 to 6, with many repeats, it agrees with Python's bisect.bisect_left for x from 0 to 7.
tests.message: Stopped on line 4, in bisect_left: The code ran for too long and was stopped. Is there a loop that never ends, or code that runs a very large number of times?

tests.name: test_edges
tests.description: An empty list gives 0, x below every item gives 0, x above every item gives len(xs), and x equal to an end gives that end's slot.
tests.message: Stopped on line 6, in bisect_left: The code ran for too long and was stopped. Is there a loop that never ends, or code that runs a very large number of times?

tests.name: test_looks
tests.description: On a sorted list of a million even numbers it gives the right slots, looking at no more than 21 different items each time.
tests.message: bisect_left looked at items of a list of a million more than 100 times, where halving needs about 20. Check that every pass makes the gap hi - lo smaller.
